sections.html:
Richardson County is the southeast corner of Nebraska. Missouri lies across the river to the east and Kansas to the south, and the state's lowest point is where the Missouri River leaves Nebraska. The county covers 555 square miles, most of it farmed, and the Big Nemaha River and its branches cross the rolling hills on the way to the Missouri.

Falls City is the county seat, and Humboldt is the other city. Eight villages round out the map: Barada, Dawson, Preston, Rulo, Salem, Shubert, Stella and Verdon. Parts of the Ioway and Sac and Fox reservations sit in the southeast corner, and the village of Preston is inside the Sac and Fox reservation. If a parcel is near that area, ask the assessor and a title company how it is classified before you list.

The 2020 census counted 7,871 residents. Median age was 47.2, and 24.9% of residents were 65 or older, so a fair number of houses pass to heirs. An heir who lives out of state and inherits a house in Dawson, Stella or Verdon faces the same bill and the same deadlines as an owner next door.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects the tax
sections.html:
The treasurer is at 1700 Stone Street, Room 105, Falls City, NE 68355, phone 402-245-3511. Current and back real estate tax can be looked up and paid online through MIPS Inc. The online fee is 2.35 percent on a card with a $2.00 minimum, or $1.00 for an e-check.

Drainage taxes are the exception. They cannot be paid online, so ask the treasurer for the full balance, drainage items included, before you set a closing date.

StepDate or rule
First half delinquentMay 1 (Statute 77-204)
Second half delinquentSeptember 1
Valuation protestOn or before June 30, with the County Clerk
Board decision mailedBy August 2
Appeal to the state commissionBy August 24
County tax saleFirst Monday in March, 9:00 a.m.

The assessor's office is at 1700 Stone Street, Room 102, phone 402-245-4012, open from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, through lunch. It sets fair and equitable value on real and personal property, keeps the parcel maps and prepares the tax roll that the treasurer bills from. Staff attend every Board of Equalization meeting and review applications for homestead exemptions and for religious, charitable and educational exemptions.

A protest goes on Form 422 to the County Clerk by June 30, one form for each parcel. Give your reasons, the value you want and documents the board can use to reach it. Under Statute 77-1502, late or incomplete protests are dismissed.

If the board's ruling goes against you, the Tax Equalization and Review Commission takes appeals filed by August 24. A recent appraisal or a contractor's estimate for needed repairs makes a stronger case than an opinion alone.

sections.h2: How the county tax sale works
sections.html:
The county sells tax certificates the first Monday in March at 9:00 a.m. at the courthouse. The delinquent list is advertised for three consecutive weeks in February and posted online, and the county also posts a list of parcels that went unsold.

  • Buyers register by the Friday before the sale and pay $25 to register.
  • The county charges $25 for each certificate sold.
  • The redemption period is three years, at 14 percent.
  • After three years without redemption, the buyer has six months to foreclose.

A parcel that did not sell is still delinquent. If yours is on the unsold list, the tax is still owed and needs a plan.

Falls City Public Schools runs two elementary schools, a junior high and Falls City High School. Humboldt Table Rock Steinauer Public Schools, Auburn Public Schools, Johnson-Brock Public Schools and Pawnee City Public Schools also reach into the county, and Sacred Heart School in Falls City is a Catholic K to 12 school. The district a house falls in drives the school levy, so check the district on your statement.
Buyers will ask about hail or wind damage, and a claim on file tells them more than the age of the roof does. Keep any repair invoices and insurance paperwork together so you can answer plainly.

The title company gets the tax payoff from the treasurer and takes it from your proceeds. You also pay the documentary stamp tax, which the register of deeds collects at $3.32 per $1,000 of value on deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026. Form 521 goes with the deed.

If the house is inherited, in disrepair or behind on taxes, tell us the address and parcel number. We will go through the numbers with you, with no obligation. A cash sale skips the buyer's loan, so the schedule depends on title work and the payoff, not on a lender.

faqs.q: When are Richardson County property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: The first half becomes delinquent May 1 and the second half September 1, under Nebraska Statute 77-204.

faqs.q: Can I pay Richardson County taxes online?
faqs.a: Yes, through MIPS Inc., with a 2.35 percent card fee ($2.00 minimum) or a $1.00 e-check fee. Drainage taxes cannot be paid online, so call 402-245-3511.

faqs.q: Where do I file a protest in Richardson County?
faqs.a: File Form 422 with the County Clerk on or before June 30, one protest per parcel. The assessor's office can be reached at 402-245-4012.

faqs.q: When is the Richardson County tax sale?
faqs.a: It is held the first Monday in March at 9:00 a.m. at the courthouse, after three weeks of advertising in February.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem after a Richardson County tax sale?
faqs.a: Three years. After that the certificate holder has six months to foreclose, and the certificates carry 14 percent interest.
